thread.title: UPRO Approaching Bear Market Territory, Money Management Is Key - ProShares UltraPro S&P 500 ETF (NYSEARCA:UPRO)

author: Todd Akin
title: UPRO Approaching Bear Market Territory, Money Management Is Key - ProShares UltraPro S&P 500 ETF (NYSEARCA:UPRO)
text:
The ProShares UltraPro S&P 500 ETF ( UPRO ) has fallen over 40% from its highs recently of around $59 per share, which is equivalent to almost a 15% correction in the overall SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ), and this is forcing some investors to ask tough questions about their portfolios.
Does one simply buy the 15% dip in the longest bull market in history, which is considered a healthy pullback? Or, do you avoid catching a falling knife, as the bear market everyone has feared is finally upon us?
The dilemma right now for UPRO lies in the fact that, while it has fallen a decent amount from its highs, shares have just broken one-year support. On top of this bearish development, there is still a large amount of downside left in this market before the next support level comes into play.
Therefore, UPRO is in no man’s land territory, and buying right now is a tricky proposition for investors unless disciplined money management strategies are employed. In order to prevent myself from getting burned in this market, for example, a strategy to pyramid into UPRO needs to be devised. These strategies will be discussed below.
UPRO Overview UPRO’s expense ratio of .92% is rather low considering the fact that it is leveraged. However, investing in leveraged ETFs can be risky since various instruments are used, such as options and derivatives, to accomplish these goals. Here is the official description of UPRO:
The investment seeks daily investment results- before fees and expenses- that correspond to three times (3x) the daily performance of the S&P 500-® Index. The fund invests in financial instruments that ProShare Advisors believes- in combination- should produce daily returns consistent with the fund's investment objective. The index is a measure of large-cap U.S. stock market performance. The fund is non-diversified.
Warning: Leveraged exchange-traded funds (ETFs) are designed to achieve their investment objective on a daily basis meaning that they are not designed to track the underlying index over an extended period of time. Leverage can increase volatility. Inverse ETFs attempt to deliver returns that are the opposite of the underlying index's returns. Typically, the longer you hold a Leveraged or Inverse ETF, the greater your potential loss.
Accordingly, Leveraged and Inverse ETFs may not be suitable for investors who plan to hold positions for longer than one trading session. These products are designed for highly experienced traders who understand their risks, including the impact of daily compounding of leveraged investment returns, and who actively monitor their positions throughout the trading day. Please read the Prospectus carefully before making your final investment decision.
Now that we have established what UPRO does, a quick macro rundown is necessary before moving on to determining our future buy points and position sizes.
Without spending too much time on the subject, the U.S. economy continues to be strong as GDP is growing at a steady pace, employment rates are high, and interest rates are still relatively low on a historical basis. Gas prices are also cheap and will act as a tailwind to the U.S. economy, which is 70% consumer driven.
The only cons that I see in the economy are rising rates, and the possibilities of slowing global activity that could occur from trade wars between the U.S. and China. However, it is in Trump’s best interest to keep positive relations with China since it helps U.S. businesses, and props the stock market up (these items are vital to Trump’s re-election chances).
The other risks seen are the sobering facts that many holdings in the S&P 500 have yet to make their corrections like others in the market have. Companies such as Boeing ( BA ), Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Netflix ( NFLX ), and even energy companies like EOG Resources ( EOG ) (which has not run up as much as others), all have significant downside left in shares.
This is why significant downside lies beneath current levels in the S&P 500, and why UPRO could see $30 in a heartbeat. Let’s take a look at the charts below to gain a better perspective.
Chart Technicals: One-Year Time Frame As investors can see by the one-year time frame below, the key support area of $40 was just broken, which is a bearish signal. Source: E*TRADE
Not only was one-year support on UPRO broken, but the RSI needs to come down more. Sure, UPRO is showing that it is oversold with an RSI of 40. However, this RSI reading applies only to the leveraged ETF, and this can be misleading because the indicators are skewed.
We will address this error in the RSI readings in a moment. First, let’s take a look at a longer-term time frame of UPRO for more clarity.
UPRO On A Max Time Frame Judging by the chart below, UPRO has had a sizable correction. But, there is clearly room to fall further. $30 looks to be the next support area, which is only $5 points away at the 200-day moving average. This also happens to be the old breakout level from 2017, which strengthens the support area. Source: E*TRADE
UPRO’s RSI is also nearly oversold at 40, which lines up with the one-year chart’s RSI reading of around 40. It is important to have the RSI line up on all time frames. However, one has to be sure that they are interpreting the data correctly. In order to see the true relative strength of the S&P 500, one must look at the single leveraged ETF, or the SPY.
S&P 500 Parent ETF As investors can see below, the SPY has broken key support on the 20-day moving average. There appears to be almost 20% downside left from current levels before reaching any form of support, which is around $200 a share, or the 2016 consolidation area. Source: E*TRADE
The RSI on SPY is also nowhere near being oversold, as it still remains at 50. This proves that UPRO’s technical indicators are skewed, and that more downside is left in this market before selling conditions become exhausted.
If investors look at the VIX Volatility Index (seen below), they will see that this also has room to rise before getting overbought. While the economy remains strong by all accounts (which is why interest rates are being raised), the QE effects on interest rates for the last ten years have been so accommodating that it remains to be seen how the unwinding process could unfold without inflicting damage.
Source: E*TRADE
In other words, some economists believe a black swan event could occur at any moment now as the Federal Reserve pulls back the curtain on their interest rate policy. People fear that the supposed tampering of interest rates could go awry, and this could make the VIX pop to 2016 levels again.
This is all speculation at this point, as no one really knows what the Fed will do beyond their last two supposed rate hikes that are coming in the future. This is why money management, and buying in wide ranges is key.
Conclusion UPRO has had a significant correction from the highs, notching around a 40% decline from former highs, which is equivalent to almost a 15% correction in the overall S&P 500. This is a good enough excuse to start pyramiding into a position. However, one has to buy in wide nets and stick to his/her buy points.
From what we could infer from the charts, starting a position in UPRO at $35 with a quarter of a position here, and then building to half a position at $30 makes sense risk/reward wise. After all, the upside would be almost 100% at $59 and the downside, while still showing chances of a 60% fall (20% on SPY), the dollar loss would be minimal since only half of a position was purchased.
If and when UPRO drops below $30 to the $20s, I will look to fill the other half of the position, and publish new updates accordingly.
